findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma` is used but never imported -- the package does not compile
packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Persists the zod `safeParse` envelope as `credential.key` instead of the token
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Both computed keys evaluate to `"[object Object]"`; schema strips every field except `access_token`
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59 — Admin guard sits on the branch where `teamId` is provably always null; team credential needs only membership
packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — In sync mode a `fetch` `Response` is persisted as the credential key, erasing the tokens
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Secret check is fail-open when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset or empty

- `prisma.credential.update` is called in the new refresh block, but `grep -n prisma` on the file returns only that line; the import block ends at line 20. `tsc` fails with "Cannot find name 'prisma'". Every sibling that writes credentials imports it (`googlecalendar:11`, `hubspot:14`, `office365calendar:9`). Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`. This is unconditional -- not gated on any flag -- and it means the entire new Salesforce block has never executed, so nothing else in it has been exercised in practice.

- `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `{success, data}` wrapper (`parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29`), but the line it replaced (`googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`) returned the flat token. The wrapper is written straight to the DB at line 100. On the next request the constructor runs `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 against that shape and throws, so the user's Google Calendar breaks permanently on the first token refresh and only a disconnect/reconnect recovers it. Not gated on credential sharing -- this is the default path for every deployment. Fix by returning `.data` from the helper (see #18).

- `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both stringify to the literal `"[object Object]"`, so the second overwrites the first and the schema reduces to `{access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional()}`. Three reviewers verified this by execution against zod 3.25: `safeParse({access_token, expiry_date, refresh_token, scope}).data` returns `{access_token}` alone. Both inline comments describe behavior the code does not have. This is the root cause of #8, #13, and #22. Replace with `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()`.

- The `if (state?.teamId)` branch creates a team-wide credential after checking only accepted membership (no role filter) and returns at line 56, so `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` at line 59 is reachable only when `state?.teamId` is falsy -- it is always called with `teamId: null`. Since `state` is an unsigned `JSON.parse` of a query param (#20), any MEMBER-role user can complete an OAuth flow with a chosen `teamId` and install their own Stripe/HubSpot/Salesforce account as the team's credential. Move the guard inside the team branch and drop the redundant membership query.

- `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response` in the sync branch, but this call site annotates it `: HubspotToken` and reads `.expiresIn`. Verified in Node: `Response.expiresIn` is `undefined`, so `expiryDate` becomes `NaN` and `JSON.stringify` of the object yields `{"expiryDate":null}` -- which line 198 writes as `credential.key`, irreversibly erasing the HubSpot tokens. The surrounding `catch (e) { this.log.error(e) }` swallows the follow-on failure, so the caller sees success. Fixed by resolving #7.

- `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` evaluates `undefined !== undefined` (or `"" !== ""`, since `.env.example` ships an empty default) as `false` when both the header and the env var are absent, skipping the 403. Past that guard nothing is user-scoped: the caller names an arbitrary `userId` and overwrites that user's credentials. Fail closed on a missing secret and compare in constant time. Confidence is 75 rather than 100 because `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` lives in `@calcom/lib/constants`, which is outside this checkout -- if that flag independently requires the secret, this degrades to a defense-in-depth gap. Confirm before merge.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — Returns a branch-dependent shape behind `() -> any`, so callers cannot satisfy both branches
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — Literal `"refresh_token"` sentinel overwrites the real refresh token and is persisted
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Gate omits `userId`, so team credentials and Salesforce get the stripping schema despite never using the sync endpoint
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:106 — Builds the connection from the stale pre-refresh token, discarding the one just fetched
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Unconditional token grant plus DB write on every service construction, no expiry gate
packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — webex / lark / office365video wired to sync but still validate against provider-native schemas
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:98 — `instance_url` stripped from the persisted key under sync; next connection targets `undefined`
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:78 — Decrypted keys persisted unvalidated, silently overwriting a user-consented credential, then 200
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Outbound sync request carries no secret or signature, while the inbound webhook requires one
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:57 — Constructor stores a now-network-bound promise with no rejection handler
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:77 — Update branch rewrites `key` only and never clears `invalid`
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:22 — Throws on failure yet returns a `safeParse` envelope, leaving dead `.success` branches at two call sites

- `refreshFunction: () -> any` collapses the inferred return to `any`, hiding that the sync branch yields a `fetch` `Response` while the fallback yields whatever the provider closure returned. Four callers survive by coincidence (their closures also return a `Response`); Google reads `res?.data` and HubSpot asserts `: HubspotToken`, and both break the moment sync is enabled. Type it `(refreshFunction: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>` -- that converts #5 and Google's failure into compile errors, which is the right outcome.

- When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper writes the literal string `"refresh_token"`, which Outlook then spreads over the live credential and persists (`office365calendar:264,270`). Previously zod omitted the absent optional key so the spread preserved the stored token; now it is clobbered. If sync is ever disabled or the endpoint retired, the next refresh posts `refresh_token=refresh_token`, gets `invalid_grant`, and the integration is dead with no recovery path and nothing logged. Delete the sentinel and let the caller's spread preserve the existing token. Adversarial refuted this for Salesforce specifically -- line 98 explicitly restores `credentialKey.refresh_token`, so the sentinel never lands there.

- `refreshOAuthTokens` requires `... && userId` to route to the sync endpoint, but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` gates on the two globals only. So a team credential (`userId === null`) and every Salesforce refresh still hit the real provider, receive a complete token response, and then have it validated by the stripping schema and stamped with the sentinel. Thread `userId` through so both predicates match exactly.

- Line 98 persists `accessTokenParsed.data`, but lines 105-107 build the `jsforce.Connection` from `credentialKey`, the snapshot read at line 73 before the refresh. The request that paid for the round trip still authenticates with the old token. Use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and `.instance_url`.

- The refresh runs from the constructor with no `isExpired` guard, unlike every sibling in this same diff (`googlecalendar:125`, `office365calendar:279`, `larkcalendar:51`, `webex:46`). Each availability lookup and booking now costs a Salesforce OAuth round trip plus an `UPDATE` on the same credential row -- added p99 latency, dead-tuple churn, row-lock serialization on concurrent bookings, and exposure to Salesforce's per-app token rate limit and concurrent-token cap. Combined with #10 the work is pure waste.

- These three got the `refreshOAuthTokens` wrapper without the matching `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Webex's schema requires `scope: z.literal("spark:kms meeting:schedules_read meeting:schedules_write")` plus `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`, none of which the documented sync payload ("only the access token and expiry date") provides -- so enabling sync makes Webex reject on every refresh. Lark reads its own `data.data.*` envelope. Either adapt per app or gate unsupported apps out explicitly rather than half-wiring them.

- Salesforce is the only app that calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse` without `refreshOAuthTokens`, so with sync on, a complete Salesforce response is stripped to `{access_token}` and persisted. The read path is a bare `as unknown as ExtendedTokenResponse` cast with no validation, so nothing throws -- line 105 just passes `instanceUrl: undefined` to jsforce and every call fails far from the write that caused it.

- Whatever the ciphertext decrypts to is written to `credential.key` with no schema check, and `findFirst({userId, appId})` picks whichever credential comes first, with no marker distinguishing sync-managed rows from user-consented ones. A user who connected their own Google account through the UI can have it silently repointed, with the endpoint answering `200 Credentials updated`. This is the green-while-red failure: the operator's sync job is green while the user's bookings 500 on a `googleCredentialSchema.parse` far downstream.

- The POST carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no `headers` key at all. To function, the self-hoster's endpoint must therefore return a live access token for any user id any caller names -- so anything that can reach it enumerates `calcomUserId=1..N` and harvests tokens. The asymmetry is the trap: this PR adds `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` for the inbound direction, so operators will reasonably assume the outbound call is authenticated too. Send the same secret and document that the endpoint must verify it.

- `this.conn = this.getClient(credential).then((c) => c);` attaches only a fulfillment handler, and `getClient` now has five new rejection sources (fetch, `response.json()`, the `HttpError` throw, the helper's throw, the DB write). If the service is constructed but never awaited -- which happens when Cal.com enumerates credentials and exercises only some -- an unhandled rejection takes down the process, escalating one degraded integration into a web-process restart.

- Healing a broken credential is the endpoint's main purpose, but the update writes `key` only. Google's refresh path in this same diff sets `invalid: true` on a credential; nothing here resets it. The operator pushes fresh keys, gets `200`, and the integration stays dead. Add `invalid: false` to the update payload.

- The helper throws at line 22 and then returns the `safeParse` result, so every value it returns has `success === true`. `salesforce:92-94` is unreachable, and `office365calendar:264`'s `(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` guard is permanently the right-hand side -- while #2 shows what happens when a caller forgets the unwrap entirely. Return `.data` and delete the dead guards.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — In sync mode a `fetch` `Response` is persisted as the credential key, erasing the tokens

adjudication.rationale: Real problem: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code assigns that return value to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and (in the existing flow of `refreshAccessToken`) expects token fields from it. In sync mode, those fields won’t exist because it’s a `Response` (not parsed JSON / not a HubspotToken), which will break token handling and can lead to persisting/using invalid token data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Secret check is fail-open when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset or empty

adjudication.rationale: The handler rejects only when the header value is not equal to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (so it is `undefined`), and the request omits the header (so `req.headers[...]` is also `undefined`), the comparison becomes `undefined !== undefined` which is false, so the request is accepted. That is a verifiable fail-open path in the diff. (If the secret is set to an empty string, it’s not the same fail-open condition, but it still becomes trivially satisfiable by sending an empty header.)
